state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a cardboard cutout of a circle and a triangle. When you fold them along the lines, which shape would each net create? This can help you visualize how the 2D shapes transform into 3D shapes.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you're saying, but I'm still a bit confused. So, if I fold the circle, it would make a sphere, right? But what about the triangle? I’m not sure how that one fits in. Can you explain that part again?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a paper cone and a paper pyramid. When you fold them along the lines, which shape would each net create? This can help you see how the 2D shapes transform into 3D shapes.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher fails to address the student's specific confusion about the circle-sector net (which forms a cone), provides mathematically problematic guidance (suggesting a circle folds into a sphere), and when the student expresses continued confusion, simply repeats a similar prompt without clarifying the actual net shown or correcting the sphere misconception.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, everyday analogies (cardboard cutouts, paper cones and pyramids) to help the student visualize the abstract concept of how 2D nets fold into 3D shapes, which is a textbook example of the experiential strategy.
